newsitem.title: USA: L.A. sanitation district says landfill stays open.
newsitem.headline: L.A. sanitation district says landfill stays open.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Sanitation District said on Friday it received court approval to continue operation of a major landfill after a long legal challenge to the project.
The Puente Hills Landfill had met opposition from a local homeowners' association, a school district and a commercial real estate developer.
The sanitation district said that a ruling by the Second District Court of Appeal allows the landfill to continue to serve more than 60 cities for waste diversion and disposal.

In its decision, the Second District Court of Appeal in Los Angeles approved the environmental impact report on the expansion of the Puente Hills Landfill. The court also found that the permits for the landfill fully complied with the California Environmental Quality Act.
The decision affirms earlier rulings allowing the landfill to continue operation until the year 2003.

"The court's decision today underscores a growing judicial concern that the rules regulating the protection of the environment not be misused as a procedural instrument to block or delay environmentally sound projects that have complied with all health and safety requirements and serve the needs of the community," the sanitation district's legal counsel, Daniel V. Hyde, said in a statement.
The Puente Hills Landfill currently receives about a third of the county's solid waste.
